General config options for the mod
General config options for the mod
Options which may conflict with other mods or resource packs. You may need to disable some of these when using Particle Interactions in combination with other mods for the best experience
eg_particle_interactions.config.global_o: Pixel consistent block / item particles

Makes the particles that appear when mining blocks, placing blocks, or eating food be pixel consistent.

Try disabling this if you are having visual issues with other mods or resourcepacks
Particle z-fighting fix

Fixes particles z-fighting (glitching) with each-other when looking downwards, MC-91873 on the bug tracker. This fix isn't perfect but it works for most cases.

This fix works by moving the particle upwards slightly when landing on a block to mitigate z-fighting. Note: This option only applies to particles from vanilla and most other mods, Particle Interactions' particles use a different fix for z-fighting which renders each particle at a slightly different y value.

Disable this if particles from other mods are acting weirdly or not moving correctly. You may also want to disable this if you have another mod that also fixes this issue
Projectile particle velocity fix
Makes thrown egg and snowball impact particles have more velocity similar to what they had around Minecraft 1.12
Auto collapse config menu lists

Should lists in the config menu be collapsed by default?

Enabling this is useful if your config has very long lists of blocks / fluids / etc.
This doesn't take effect until you close and re-open the config menu
Firefly fixes

Fixes some annoying issues with firefly particles when enabled:
 - Fireflies won't die in any block other than air (yes, they die in flowers or grass in vanilla!)
 - Fireflies won't get stuck in place on the floor or underside of blocks (once you notice this, you cant unsee it)
Show config button in options screen
If enabled, a button to open this config screen is added in the options screen if mod menu is not installed
Config options that may have an impact on performance
Toggles for certain particle behaviours that can have a performance impact
eg_particle_interactions.config.global_o: §oRender Distance:§r Interaction Particles

The maximum distance in chunks that particles spawned from block, item, or entity interactions are visible from.

High values may result in worse performance, the final render distance is capped at Minecraft's render distance
§oRender Distance:§r Block Particles

The maximum distance in chunks that block breaking or placement particles are visible from.

High values may result in worse performance, the final render distance is capped at Minecraft's render distance
§oRender Distance:§r Ambient Particles

The maximum distance in chunks that ambient particles are visible from. This includes particles that arent included in the previous two render distance settings, such as ambient fire embers.

High values may result in worse performance, the final render distance is capped at Minecraft's render distance
Particle fluid reactivity

Whether or not particles can interact with fluids in the world.

May improve performance when a lot of particles are in the world around fluids
Particle bounce physics
May slightly improve performance when a lot of particles are in the world
Allow additional particle emissions

Whether or not particles can spawn other particles occasionally.

May improve performance when a lot of particles are in the world or if you are reaching the particle limit
CAUTION: Don't change these options unless you have been told to or know what you are doing
eg_particle_interactions.config.global_o: Show particle emitter bounds

Visualises particle emitter bounding boxes with a particle in the bottom north-west corner and top south-east corner.

This will be disabled the next time you open the game
Show particle tick position

Renders a green bounding box visualising a particles tick position and collision size. Also renders a pink square when the particle is in the air, or purple when on the ground.

This will be disabled the next time you open the game
Show particle render position

Renders a red bounding box visualising a particles render culling box.

This will be disabled the next time you open the game
Log extra particle packet error info

Logs extra debugging information to the log if an error occurs while handling client-bound particle packets.

This will be disabled the next time you open the game
Texture palette logging

Logs extra debugging information about texture palettes.

This will be disabled the next time you open the game

§lVanilla-like§r
Uses the vanilla particles when brushing a block. If the block has a Block Particle Override then that will be spawned instead.

§lDust§r
Spawns a dust particle when brushing a block. If the block has a Block Particle Override then that will be spawned instead.

§lDisabled§r
Disables the brushing particles entirely
